evidence.notes: `build_nat_prelude` admits `Nat.land_div_two` (`nat_prelude/land_div_two.rs`) through the trusted `Kernel::add_declaration` gate. `nat_theorem_inventory`'s rendered type is `(x0 x1 : AxNat) -> Eq (div (land x0 x1) 2) (land (div x0 2) (div x1 2))`, matching this fact's `formal.statement` up to variable naming. notes: Proved in Axeyum by a NEW kernel theorem, `Nat.land_div_two` (`nat_prelude/land_div_two.rs`), dualizing `land_low_bit.rs`'s `land_mod_two_eq_mul` technique: that proof erases the higher recursive term by taking `mod _ 2` of the succ-row's `2*rec+bit` shape; this one erases the LOW bit by taking `div _ 2` of the SAME shape (`div_two_mul_add_of_lt`, sharing `parity.rs`'s `mod_two_mul_add_of_lt`'s `div_mod_unique` witness construction but projecting the quotient component instead of the remainder). What remained was showing the erased recursive term (fuel = the succ-row's predecessor) equals the CANONICAL `land (div a 2) (div b 2)` (fuel = the half itself) via the already-proved fuel-irrelevance lemma `Nat.land_aux_agree_of_fuel`, needing only `Le half_a pa`, which `half_le_predecessor_of_succ` gives directly at `k := pa` via `le_refl`. Mathlib's `&&&` for `Nat` is `Nat.land`, so reconciling this `and_div_two` mirror to `Nat.land_div_two` is honest under the mirror-flip criterion in CLAUDE.md.
